  escapeYAMLValue. escapeYAMLValue caps at maxContractFieldRunes (500) and
  is documented as bounding adversarial email-derived metadata
  (message_id/from/subject). cmd.Prompt is neither adversarial nor short: it
  comes from a GPG-signed command file authored by the recipe authorizer,
  and it becomes the mission's success_criteria -- the worker's actual task
  instructions. The 500-rune cap silently truncates it mid-sentence with no
  marker and no log. Observed live: a spawned worker reported its own
  success_criteria was cut off mid-word.

  escapeYAMLPipe (internal/daemon/mission.go line ~76) already performs
  identical escaping with no length cap, for exactly this reason ("pipe data
  can be up to 1MB"). Use it for cmd.Prompt. Update its doc comment so it
  describes its real role -- uncapped escaping for trusted, potentially-long
  content -- rather than naming only pipe output. Leave escapeYAMLValue and
  its 500-rune cap alone: that cap is correct for the adversarial metadata
  fields it was written for.

  work with no log line, so an operator sees a pipeline that simply did not
  reply and has nothing to diagnose from.
    - pipeline.go ~line 178, auto-reply: `if err := ValidateArgs(...); err

      logs a warning with the error, matching the sibling

      nil { return }` -- bare return, no log.
    - pipeline.go ~line 381, fireElse: `runner, ok := e.Runners[...]; if !ok

  following the field conventions already used in this file.

  - the generated contract still parses as valid YAML and is still accepted by the real ethos CLI (TestBuildStageContract_ValidatesAgainstRealEthosCLI passes)
  - go test -race -count=1 ./... passes; test count does not decrease

leader: claude
worker: adb
evaluator:
  handle: kth
inputs:
  ticket: beadle-axj
context: |
  Design a repeatable test tier for beadle-daemon's mail-triggered pipeline.
  This is a DESIGN mission: produce a design document, not an implementation.

  WHY THIS EXISTS. The daemon path (email arrives -> trust classification ->
  per-contact permission -> planner -> executor -> runner -> ethos mission
  create -> worker spawn) had never actually run until a manual live test
  this week. That one run surfaced four real defects, including a mission
  contract shape that ethos's real schema rejects outright (beadle-8gt) --
  every daemon-triggered mission would have failed. The path is now the
  foundation for upcoming work, so it needs coverage that is deterministic,
  runs identically for a developer and in CI, and would have caught
  beadle-8gt.

  THE HARD CONSTRAINT -- dev/CI parity, no environment-dependent branches.
  A test that silently skips locally is the same failure as one that skips
  in CI: the operator believes the path is covered and it is not. That is
  precisely how beadle-8gt shipped. So:
    - No t.Skip on a missing dependency. If a required tool is absent the
      test FAILS with a message naming what to install.
    - One entry point. The tier runs under `make check`; CI invokes that
      same target. No CI-only invocation, no separate flag or build tag.
    - Zero dependence on ambient developer state. It must behave identically
      on a maintainer's machine and a clean CI runner.
    - Fast enough to sit in the pre-commit gate, since `make check` runs
      before every commit.

  MATERIAL THAT ALREADY EXISTS -- survey it before proposing anything new:
    - internal/testserver.Fixture: in-process IMAP+SMTP, no real network.
      AddRawMessage(folder, raw []byte) accepts arbitrary RFC822 bytes, so
      any trust level can be induced directly -- Proton internal headers
      (X-Pm-Content-Encryption / X-Pm-Origin) for `trusted`, a real
      multipart/signed body for `verified`/`untrusted`, neither for
      `unverified`.
    - internal/daemon.Spawner is an interface; WorkerSpawner is the only
      implementation and it execs a real `claude` subprocess. That single
      seam is the one thing that should stay faked.
    - isolatedEthosEnv in internal/daemon/pipeline_test.go: the established
      pattern for exec'ing the real ethos CLI without mutating the shared
      global ~/.punt-labs/ethos tree. Read its doc comment -- it encodes a
      real corruption incident.
    - docs/TESTING.md: the existing pyramid this tier must slot into, and
      the ephemeral-GNUPGHOME and short-/tmp/bg-* socket-path rules.
    - .github/workflows/test.yml: does NOT install ethos today, which is why
      the beadle-8gt regression test skips on every CI run (beadle-axj).

  WHAT THE TIER MUST PIN DOWN. The daemon's security-relevant behavior is a
  sequence of gates; each deserves independent coverage, including its
  negative case:
    1. Trust classification -- OnNewMail admits only Verified/Trusted; the
       lower two rungs create no mission.
    2. Per-contact permission -- contacts.CheckPermission's `x` bit gates
       mission creation; a perfectly verified message from an ungranted
       sender unlocks nothing.
    3. Command-file signature -- LoadCommands rejects unsigned/tampered
       recipes, and an absent or ambiguous daemon.json disables command
       loading entirely (zero commands, not unsigned fallback).
    4. Contract validity -- the generated contract is accepted by the REAL
       ethos CLI. This is the gate that beadle-8gt broke, and only a real
       exec catches it; a hand-rolled string or struct assertion does not.

  DECISIONS THE DESIGN MUST MAKE AND JUSTIFY:
    - Where the harness lives: unexported helpers inside package daemon, a
      new internal/ test-support package, or something else. Name the
      tradeoff (a shared package is importable by other packages' tests but
      cannot touch daemon's unexported surface).
    - The assertion surface a future test author writes against -- what a
      new gate test costs to add. Cheap-to-extend is the point; this exists
      to make building on the daemon path predictable.
    - How `ethos` is pinned and installed so dev and CI agree on one version
      number, following the GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION pin pattern in
      punt-kit/standards/go.md (one variable, referenced by the Makefile
      tools target, the lint/check target, and the CI workflow).
    - Whether the daemon's poll loop is driven or bypassed. Note the real
      constraint: Poller.loop's first poll never fires the new-mail callback
      (see internal/email/poller.go), and the minimum poll interval is 1m --
      a test cannot wait on wall-clock polling.
    - What stays real and what gets faked, with the reasoning per seam. The
      default is real; each fake must earn its place.

  Do not write implementation code. Do not modify CI, the Makefile, or any
  Go file. Produce the design and the ADR text.
success_criteria:

  - The design states explicitly, per gate, which negative case is covered and how the trust level or signature state is induced
  - The design shows the exact dev and CI invocation and demonstrates they are the same target, with no skip path on a missing dependency
  - The design names the ethos version-pin mechanism and every file that must reference the single pinned value
  - The design accounts for Poller's first-poll callback suppression and the 1m minimum interval, and states how the tier avoids waiting on wall-clock polling
  - A proposed DESIGN.md ADR entry is drafted at the end of the doc, ready for the leader to paste at merge time
  - Every claim about existing behavior cites file:line in this repo; no assertion about testserver, Spawner, Poller, or isolatedEthosEnv is made without reading the source
  - markdownlint passes on the new doc
  - Commit incrementally -- one commit per logical step. Each commit must pass `make check`. Do not accumulate more than 30 minutes of uncommitted changes.

  rounds: 2
